messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5 × Jupiter’s radius** (about 18,000 km). Its mass is estimated to be around 10–20 M_J, placing it at the upper end of the “super‑Jupiter” category.  

> **Why it’s the biggest known**  
> - It was discovered using direct imaging, which allows astronomers to measure its size directly.  
> - Its radius is larger than any other confirmed exoplanet, and its mass is close to the deuterium‑burning limit (~13 M_J), beyond which objects are usually classified as brown dwarfs rather than planets.

> **Note on the definition**  
> The boundary between massive planets and brown dwarfs is somewhat fuzzy. Some objects just above the deuterium‑burning threshold are still called “planets” if they formed in a protoplanetary disk, while others are classified as brown dwarfs if they formed like stars. HD 100546 b sits right at that boundary, making it the largest object we can confidently call a planet.
